articleSummary: Brucellosis in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China, is most strongly linked to livestock density. articleHeadline: New Fusarium Strain Decimated Farmed Prawns in South China, Genome Reveals
articleSummary: New Fusarium strain 1-Jan caused black gill disease in farmed Pacific whiteleg shrimp (Penaeus vannamei) in South China, triggering heavy economic losses. Diseased prawns showed black plaques on gills and dark brown ulcerative lesions on the carapace and appendages; survivors developed black gill disease within eight days. Experimental infection reproduced the disease, and the fungus was re-isolated from inoculated shrimp with identical genotype, establishing 1-Jan as the causative agent. Genome sequencing revealed a 51.8-Mb assembly across 54 scaffolds (N50 1,974 kb, GC 51.73%), with 9,769 predicted genes. PHI database identified 1,101 pathogen-host interaction hits; CAZy analysis yielded 497 annotations, including 225 glycoside hydrolases; 736 pathogenicity-factor genes with SNPs. Phylogenomic analysis placed 1-Jan on a branch with F. solani complex, most similar to Nectria haematococca and F. virguliforme. The data suggest chitin-degrading capacity may drive crustacean pathogenicity; further functional validation is needed for aquaculture risk assessment.

articleHeadline: Co-infections Worsen Outcomes in Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia
articleSummary: SFTS (severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome) due to tick-borne SFTSV was studied in 231 patients treated May 2021–June 2024 at the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University in Hefei, China. Co-infections occurred in 81 (35.1%): 47 community-acquired infections (CAIs) and 34 hospital-acquired infections (HAIs). Mortality was 23.4% for CAIs, 8.8% for HAIs, and 19.3% for those without co-infection. CAIs showed more diarrhea on admission and higher cerebral infarction history, with signs of myocardial and pancreatic injury and coagulation dysfunction (elevated troponin I, amylase/lipase, D-dimer, FDP; lower albumin). CAIs and HAIs required more ribavirin, antibiotics, antifungals, and transfusions; ICU admission and costs were higher. Pathogens were fungal-predominant, especially Aspergillus spp. and A. fumigatus; CAIs yielded 63 pathogens, HAIs 39; bacteria constituted about half, with drug-resistant organisms present. Rare viral co-infections (influenza A, HPIV). Antifungal therapy improved CAIs fungal-survival; not clearly beneficial for HAIs. Lasso regression identified CAI risk factors.

articleHeadline: Doctors suspected a rare kidney parasite -- then microscope bristles revealed the "worms" were earthworms from outside the home
articleSummary: Earthworms from the environment, not a human parasite, caused a six-month toilet mystery in a 58-year-old woman from rural China. Four motile, blood-red worms (25–35 mm) appeared in a ground-floor toilet. Initial testing for parasites—including suspicion of the giant kidney worm Dioctophyma renale, plus stool/urine/blood tests, IgE, schistosomiasis antibody, and ultrasound—were negative, and the patient had no urinary symptoms. Microscopy revealed setae (chitinous bristles) characteristic of oligochaetes, identifying the organisms as earthworms and pointing to environmental contamination (pseudoparasitism) rather than true infection. The pattern—worms appearing in the same toilet, mainly in summer to autumn, likely entering via the downpipe—supported an external source. Urine collected at home after the finding yielded no additional specimens, confirming non-infectious origin. Clinicians should look for setae, use sterile urine collection to rule out contamination, and consider environmental exposure in toilet-derived worm cases.
notes: 本事例は感染症ではなく環境由来の疑似寄生症（ミミズの誤認）であり、シグナルトリアージの対象外。

articleSummary: China-wide study of 335 Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from drug-resistance surveillance regions in patients with no prior pretomanid exposure found a baseline pretomanid resistance rate of 4.5% (15/335). articleSummary: Chandipura virus, a neurotropic vesiculovirus of Rhabdoviridae, was first isolated in Chandipura, Maharashtra, India (1965).
